hteam theme set/list now accept custom themes from
~/.config/hteam/themes/<name>.toml, on top of the built-in presets.
Each field is optional and overrides a role on top of a `base` preset,
so a custom theme only needs to declare the colors it wants to change.

saving it as active, instead of letting a broken file surface only
when the TUI opens.

TUI only themed borders/accents and left the screen on the terminal's
native background, so "custom theme" couldn't actually repaint the
whole app.

commits.message:
fix(client): parse Sept. and noon/midnight timestamps in daily-work

The timestamp regex in parse_daily_work_history assumed a 3-letter
month abbreviation and a numeric time, but Django's AP-style date
format renders September as "Sept." (4 letters) and exact noon/
midnight as "noon"/"midnight" instead of a numeric time. When the
regex failed to match, the whole history entry was silently dropped
instead of just the timestamp field, so every September event (and
any exact-noon/midnight event in other months) disappeared from
`hteam daily-work` without error.

feat(cards): add follow-up tracking with complete/cancel actions

Hteam marks cards with a scheduled follow-up via a "Follow-up" label and
already returns a precomputed urgency status (get_time_status) per card in
the list endpoint, but the client discarded it when mapping CardListEntry
to Card. The follow-up date and its complete/cancel actions aren't exposed
by any JSON API at all - they only exist in the server-rendered HTML of the
card detail page, attached to the comment marked as follow-up.

- Add Card.time_status (populated only for cards with the Follow-up label)
  and Label::is_follow_up/Card::has_follow_up helpers as the single source
  of truth for that label name
- Show a colored urgency indicator on board cards in the TUI (new
  Theme::warning/danger roles across all 3 presets, resolved from
  get_time_status text), and a "Seguimiento" column in the CLI/--json/MCP
  card listings
- Fix draw_board's card height (3 -> 4 rows), which silently clipped the
  second line of card text (labels/indicator) under Borders::ALL
- Add HteamClient::get_card_follow_up/complete_follow_up/cancel_follow_up,
  scraping the card detail page and POSTing to /followup/{id}/complete and
  /followup/{id}/cancel with the CSRF token, same as the site's own form
- Surface the follow-up date and 'v'/'x' complete/cancel actions inline
  with its comment in the TUI comments popup, loaded lazily only for cards
  that have the Follow-up label
- Add matching `hteam cards follow-up`/`follow-up-complete`/
  `follow-up-cancel` CLI commands and card_follow_up* MCP tools

merge: resolve dev <- main conflict in CHANGELOG.md/docs/changelog.json

main advanced to v0.7.0 via the release workflow while dev kept
accumulating unreleased work (theme presets, self-update, the
September/noon timestamp fix, and follow-up tracking) on a separate
line of history not reachable from the v0.7.0 tag. A plain 3-way merge
mis-bucketed those dev-only commits under the already-released [0.7.0]
section instead of [Unreleased], and docs/changelog.json (a single-line
generated file) conflicted outright.

Resolved by regenerating both files with git-cliff scoped to the
v0.7.0..dev commit range (the same invocation changelog.yml uses) and
splicing that as a fresh [Unreleased] entry on top of main's untouched,
already-released history — instead of trusting a full regenerate against
the merge commit, which reproduces the same mis-bucketing due to the
diamond-shaped history.

commits.message:
ci(release): fix gh release create race and skip-when-nothing-to-bump

- Drop --verify-tag on gh release create: the tag is always pushed by
  this same job right before this step, so verification is redundant
  and can hit GitHub's matching-refs API before it reflects the tag
  just pushed, aborting with "no matches found for".
- Don't fail when there's nothing to bump: ci/chore/docs/style/test/
  build-only commits are skipped by git-cliff's bump parsers, so an
  automatic run can compute the current latest tag unchanged. Only
  fail hard when an explicit version was requested and collides with
  an existing tag.
